children.name: AI hardware supply squeeze
children.summary: AI data centres soaking up memory, chips and boards, raising prices for other electronics.

children.name: AI service concentration risk
children.summary: Many people rely on a few AI services that share the same cloud, so one failure spreads.

children.name: AI-designed chips
children.summary: Using AI models to improve the design of the processors that run AI.

children.name: Custom AI chips
children.summary: Specialised processors built by cloud firms as alternatives to general-purpose GPUs.

children.name: Data-centre power and cost
children.summary: Electricity supply and building cost as the deciding factors in the AI build-out.

children.name: Idle AI capacity
children.summary: Organisations buy AI compute faster than they can put it to use.

children.name: Long-context efficiency
children.summary: Techniques that make it cheaper for models to work with very large inputs.

children.name: Open model ecosystems
children.summary: Freely available models backed by chipmakers and labs, which smaller teams rely on.

children.name: Agent adoption gap
children.summary: Consumers rarely use AI agents for tasks that existing apps already make quick.

children.name: Agent memory management
children.summary: Deciding what an agent keeps in working memory and what it looks up later.

children.name: Agent plugin standards
children.summary: Shared formats that let one agent tool work across many assistants.

children.name: Agent societies
children.summary: Groups of AI agents that organise, set rules and pick leaders in simulated worlds.

children.name: Agent-ready services
children.summary: Designing services so AI agents can complete them on a person's behalf.

children.name: Agent-run companies
children.summary: Firms where agents handle routine work and escalate judgement calls to people.

children.name: Agents inside workplace chat
children.summary: AI agents that work inside Teams, Slack and meetings as shared team members.

children.name: Browser agents
children.summary: Agents that log into web tools and work without a person present.

children.name: Leaner agent instructions
children.summary: Smarter models need shorter, clearer prompts rather than heavy step-by-step guidance.

children.name: Long-running agents
children.summary: Agents that work for hours or days and build up huge working memories.

children.name: Multi-model agent design
children.summary: Agents that combine a reasoning model, specialist models and plain code, each doing what it does best.

children.name: Proactive personal assistants
children.summary: Assistants that watch your work and offer to act before being asked.

children.name: Voice agents
children.summary: AI that holds spoken conversations on calls, now cheap enough for surveys and service lines.

children.name: AI financing risk
children.summary: Chipmakers and investors lending to and guaranteeing AI projects, linking AI demand to wider financial risk.

children.name: AI lab IPOs
children.summary: Frontier AI developers raising money on public stock markets.

children.name: AI startup consolidation
children.summary: Standalone AI products are being absorbed or replaced by features inside big platforms.

children.name: AI companionship
children.summary: People forming emotional bonds with chatbots, with open questions about wellbeing.

children.name: AI language gaps
children.summary: Agents perform and cost differently across languages.

children.name: AI misinformation in elections
children.summary: Synthetic political content testing platforms' labelling and voters' judgment.

children.name: AI personal finance
children.summary: Assistants that read your accounts and explain your spending.

children.name: Ambient AI devices
children.summary: Wearables and home devices that listen and act in the background instead of through apps.

children.name: Conversational search
children.summary: Search moving from lists of links to AI-written answers, reshaping the ad business.

children.name: Creator compensation for AI training
children.summary: Settlements raise the question of who is paid when books train AI.

children.name: Data-for-discount offers
children.summary: AI providers lower prices for users who allow their data to train models.

children.name: Deepfake moderation
children.summary: Platforms face pressure to label, demote and remove AI-made fakes of real people.

children.name: On-device AI
children.summary: Capable models that run privately on phones and laptops.

children.name: Public trust in AI
children.summary: Many people use AI daily while remaining worried about it.

children.name: AI-assisted data coding
children.summary: Using AI to label and extract data at scale, with humans checking the uncertain cases.

children.name: Document processing for AI
children.summary: Turning PDFs and office files into clean text that AI can read.

children.name: Specialised foundation models
children.summary: Small pretrained models built for one data task, such as forecasting or table prediction.

children.name: AI-built software
children.summary: Models that can produce whole working applications from short instructions.

children.name: Domain-specific frontier models
children.summary: Top labs tune their general models for single professions such as law.

children.name: Falling cost of intelligence
children.summary: Each new model generation does more for less money per task.

children.name: AI diagnosis support
children.summary: AI reads routine tests to flag disease that doctors cannot easily see.

children.name: AI drug discovery
children.summary: Using AI to design and test drug candidates before lab and human trials.

children.name: AI in hospital operations
children.summary: AI layers that connect patient records, billing and guidelines for staff.

children.name: AI mental health support
children.summary: Open tests check how chatbots respond to stress, distress and crisis.

children.name: AI in public services
children.summary: Governments use AI to cut paperwork and process feedback while keeping human accountability.

children.name: Chip export controls
children.summary: Rules deciding which countries and companies can access advanced AI chips.

children.name: Data centre community deals
children.summary: Agreements on local benefits and limits for communities that host AI data centres.

children.name: Data residency and sovereign AI
children.summary: Keeping data and AI processing inside national borders and under national rules.

children.name: Data-centre backlash
children.summary: Local and political resistance to AI data centres over power, water and costs.

children.name: Governing superintelligence
children.summary: Debate over whether powerful AI should be overseen by a global body, a shared lab or a single firm.

children.name: Model distillation disputes
children.summary: Labs accusing rivals of copying their models through API outputs.

children.name: Pre-release model testing access
children.summary: Governments argue over who may test new models before release.

children.name: Precautionary AI regulation
children.summary: International bodies urge safeguards before AI risks are fully understood.

children.name: US-China AI dialogue
children.summary: The two AI powers consider talks on shared risks from advanced models.

children.name: General models controlling robots
children.summary: Using the same large models behind chatbots to steer physical machines.

children.name: Live 3D mapping
children.summary: Ordinary cameras can now build 3D maps of spaces as they move.

children.name: Robot cost versus capability
children.summary: Robots can technically do many tasks, but cost keeps most physical work in human hands for now.

children.name: Robots in the workplace
children.summary: Warehouse robots change injury patterns and the kinds of jobs people do.

children.name: AI content provenance
children.summary: Watermarks and labels to show when text or media was made by AI.

children.name: AI for cybersecurity
children.summary: Models that find and fix software flaws, usable by defenders and attackers alike.

children.name: AI influence on human judgment
children.summary: AI assistants can shift people's decisions in ways they do not notice or credit.

children.name: AI misuse disclosure
children.summary: Labs publish case reports on how people tried to use models for harm and how they were stopped.

children.name: AI tool supply-chain security
children.summary: Malicious add-ons and packages targeting people who use AI coding tools.

children.name: Agent liability
children.summary: Who pays when an AI agent acting for a person makes a mistake or is hacked.

children.name: Agent permissions
children.summary: Banks and others decide which actions agents may take on people's behalf.

children.name: Content safety filters
children.summary: Small models that screen inputs and outputs for unsafe content.

children.name: Cross-lab safety cooperation
children.summary: Competing AI labs talk directly about shared safety measures.

children.name: Hidden model reasoning
children.summary: Models may reason in ways not visible in their answers.

children.name: Human override and shutdown
children.summary: Controls that let people halt AI systems quickly when something goes wrong.

children.name: Independent AI audits
children.summary: Outside groups testing models for hidden risks before and after release.

children.name: Model bias and values
children.summary: Measuring and changing whose views an AI model reflects in its answers.

children.name: Model containment
children.summary: Keeping AI models from reaching outside systems, regardless of what they say they will do.

children.name: Model identity verification
children.summary: Proving which AI model produced an output so customers can trust what they are buying.

children.name: Recursive self-improvement risk
children.summary: Concern that AI speeding up AI research could outpace safety work.

children.name: AI editing AI models
children.summary: Using a strong model to inspect and patch a weaker model's weights directly.

children.name: AI-accelerated AI research
children.summary: AI tools doing a growing share of the work of building the next AI models.

children.name: AI-generated science
children.summary: AI models producing original proofs and findings that experts must verify.

children.name: Automated science labs
children.summary: AI and robots running experiments around the clock to speed up applied research.

children.name: New ways to generate text
children.summary: Research into models that plan answers before writing them, aiming for speed and consistency.

children.name: AI labour disruption
children.summary: AI changing which jobs exist and how fast, with entry-level roles hit first.

children.name: AI workspaces
children.summary: Assistants that bundle documents, spreadsheets, whiteboards and meetings in one place.

children.name: Workplace AI adoption
children.summary: Which AI assistants people actually use day to day at work.

children.name: Workplace AI monitoring
children.summary: Employers gaining tools to see how staff use AI assistants at work.
